findings.message:
[P3] Preserve login bootstrap replacement order

The app-name span is now substituted before `loginPageResponse` replaces `%%AUTH_BOOTSTRAP%%` (`passport.ts:2277-2282`). Managed project names allow `%`, so a client named `%%AUTH_BOOTSTRAP%%` causes the earlier span occurrence to consume the bootstrap replacement while the real script placeholder remains literal; `/authorize` then throws a JavaScript syntax error and the app cannot sign in. Keep the bootstrap replacement first or use a replacer callback when inserting the client name.

src/passport.ts:2277-2282

summary: The password login CSRF fix is implemented, but the authorize-page refactor introduces a template-order regression for managed project names containing the bootstrap marker.

evidence: `src/passport.ts:260-271` now issues a host-only `dua_login_csrf` cookie on login pages.
`public/auth.js:37-57` and `151-160` read that nonce and send it as `x-login-csrf-token` on password login, continuation, and registration submissions.
`src/passport.ts:887-913` rejects non-hub origins and validates the double-submit nonce; `654-733` invokes this before password authentication or session issuance.
`tests/worker_runtime.mjs:925-945` adds a sibling-origin `text/plain` regression that expects 403 with no session cookie and verifies the existing session remains.
